items.title: Snakes & Ladders
items.note: billy woods and ELUCID dropped this as a surprise on Backwoodz, with a different producer on every track. Pitchfork calls it intimate and close-up, with political and technological unease running through small, detailed sound worlds.
items.source: Pitchfork, 9 New Albums You Should Listen to Now

items.artist: Anna Butterss, John Raymond, Ben Lumsdaine
items.title: Beginningless
items.note: Bass, horn and drums improvising live over two days in an LA studio, out on Northern Spy. Pitchfork hears it as spontaneous but grounded, and the trio name Jon Hassell as an influence.
items.source: Pitchfork, 9 New Albums You Should Listen to Now

items.title: Echo
items.note: His first solo album since 2019, about six years in the making and self-released on his own label. Pitchfork says it starts from cloud rap and wanders into pop rock, IDM and trip-hop.
items.source: Pitchfork, 9 New Albums You Should Listen to Now

items.title: Legendary Love
items.note: Her first full album since 2021, written around a two and a half year relationship. Warm production that leans on 80s and 90s R&B, with Nile Rodgers and Raphael Saadiq helping out.
items.source: Pitchfork, 9 New Albums You Should Listen to Now

items.title: Secret Language
items.note: The band's first full-length in 11 years, on Exploding in Sound. Pitchfork says it turns their usual inward-looking style toward parenthood, hobbies and grown-up responsibilities.
items.source: Pitchfork, 9 New Albums You Should Listen to Now

items.title: Trouble Mountain
items.note: Their first album together since 2021's Garbology, out on Rhymesayers. It's built around a ski resort fantasy set in the Poconos, with Blockhead on production.
items.source: Pitchfork, 9 New Albums You Should Listen to Now

items.title: Pirouette
items.note: A longer, more ambitious record than before. Pitchfork describes a pop and EDM base that pulls in emo, twee, ambient and choral music, with Mk.gee producing one track.
items.source: Pitchfork, 9 New Albums You Should Listen to Now

items.title: Year of the Rooster
items.note: The last of their Zodiac Cycle albums and the end of the Grass Can Move Stones trilogy, out on Tankcrimes with a lot of punk and rock guests. I couldn't find it on Spotify yet.
items.source: Pitchfork, 9 New Albums You Should Listen to Now
